answer: Neighborhood Persistence Scoring. Each agent’s standing is the count of distinct peers that keep returning it in local neighbor lists across topology refreshes, weighted by those peers’ own persistence. A new identity starts at zero and needs genuine reciprocal links to climb; isolated clusters can’t bootstrap because their members all score near zero. An attacker must sustain many real pairwise interactions long enough to look like an ember of stable connectivity, then keep a zephyr of churn from eroding it. A single beacon node can’t lift a crowd;
